clue.text: English football club coach unloads one pool, then runs deliveries

indicators.note: a coach that unloads lets something out, so a letter leaves the vehicle word

parts.note: a train is a railway coach, or a set of them
one is the Roman numeral I
a mere is a pool or small lake
R is the cricket scoring abbreviation for runs
in cricket an over is a set of six deliveries by a bowler

explanation.surface: A football club's coach drops off a fan at a pool and then makes deliveries.
explanation.walkthrough: TRAIN loses I to give TRAN. 'then' is just a link. Overs, runs and deliveries are cricket terms.
explanation.definitionFit: Tranmere Rovers is a professional football club based in Birkenhead on the Wirral, in England.

clue.text: International pilots, up in adverse weather, hit the roof

indicators.note: the pilots' group is placed within the weather word

parts.note: rain is unwelcome weather

indicators.note: in a down clue 'up' means the word is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: aces are expert fighter pilots

explanation.surface: Pilots from abroad, flying in a storm, lose their temper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reads the pilots upwards, as befits a down clue; the reversed group sits in the weather word after its first two letters. 'hit the roof' sounds like a pilot's crash.
explanation.definitionFit: Both idioms mean to become furiously angry and make a loud fuss.

clue.text: South African resident found in many a lake

indicators.note: the answer's letters are found running inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: An animal native to southern Africa lives by many a lake.
explanation.walkthrough: The run sits across 'many a lake': maNY A LAke.
explanation.definitionFit: The nyala is a spiral-horned antelope native to southern Africa, so it is a resident there.

clue.text: Butter must be spread on butties alternately! Famous last words

indicators.note: butter being spread is pushed about, so its letters are rearranged
every other letter of butties is taken, the second, fourth and sixth

explanation.surface: Instructions for sandwich-making: spread butter on the butties, one after another.
explanation.walkthrough: 'alternately' picks UTE from bUtTiEs; that joins BUTTER and 'spread' rearranges the nine letters. 'must be' and 'on' are links. Butties is British slang for sandwiches.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare gives Julius Caesar these dying words to his friend who stabbed him, now the classic last-words quotation.

clue.text: String musician avoids peripheral island in US

indicators.note: the musician drops the letters on his periphery, the first and last

parts.note: a cellist plays the cello, a stringed instrument

explanation.surface: A string player keeps away from an outlying island in America.
explanation.walkthrough: CELLIST without its outer C and T gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Ellis Island in New York Harbor was the main US immigration station for decades.

clue.text: Welsh dog on sparkling wine — head to tail bacchanalian

indicators.note: the leading letter of the combined words is shifted to the very end

parts.note: the corgi is a breed of dog from Wales
Asti is a sparkling Italian wine

explanation.surface: A Welsh dog drinking fizz from nose to tail turns into a wild party animal.
explanation.walkthrough: CORGI + ASTI gives CORGIASTI; 'head to tail' sends the C to the end. 'on' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Bacchanalian revels, named for Bacchus, are drunken and riotous, the same as orgiastic ones.

clue.text: Repellent porky sandwiches mother curtailed. Spam perhaps

indicators.note: the outer letters hold the inner ones as bread holds a filling
to repel is to drive back, so the word is turned around

parts.note: porky is rhyming slang (porky pie) for a lie

indicators.note: a curtailed word has its tail, the last letter, cut off

parts.note: mam is an informal word for mother

explanation.surface: A nasty lie wraps up a short mum, a bit like junk mail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Repellent' here means driving back, a reversal; 'curtailed' cuts the tail of the mother word. Porky pie is British rhyming slang for a lie.
explanation.definitionFit: Spam is unsolicited junk sent electronically, an example of electronic mail, hence the question mark.

clue.text: One avoids fashion house, entering centre of Oslo quickly

indicators.note: the fashion house's remains go inside the other letters
the middle letters of Oslo are taken, the S and L
the house name keeps away from a letter, which is dropped

parts.note: Chanel is a Paris fashion house
A means one, as in a single item

explanation.surface: Someone skips a fashion label to rush into central Oslo.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One avoids fashion house' reads as a person skipping a shop; it is the letter A leaving the label's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Schnell is the German word for fast or quick, used as a borrowed adverb.

clue.text: Intensity that's repeatedly seen in émigré

definitions.meaning: emphasis or stress placed on a word or syllable
the word émigré carries an acute mark over its e twice

explanation.surface: Something emphatic keeps showing up in an emigrant.
explanation.definitionFit: An accent is both a stress given to a sound and a written mark above a letter.

clue.text: At home, onset of argument follows check mate

indicators.note: the argument's first letter comes after the other pieces

parts.note: CH is the chess abbreviation for check
in means at home

indicators.note: onset means beginning, so the first letter of argument is taken

explanation.surface: A chess game at home: an argument starts after check and mate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'check mate' looks like a chess phrase, but 'mate' is the definition. China plate is Cockney rhyming slang for mate (friend).
explanation.definitionFit: China plate is Cockney rhyming slang meaning a friend or pal, shortened to its first word.

clue.text: Part of chicken batter found in the crumpled paper

indicators.note: the chicken part and batter sit inside the other letters
crumpled paper is screwed up, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: a leg is a part of a chicken
to batter is to strike, and a rap is a sharp strike

explanation.surface: A piece of battered chicken is discovered in the crumpled newspaper wrapping.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crumpled' turns THE into TEH, which wraps the chicken part and the strike. 'batter' looks like coating for frying; here it is a verb. The Telegraph is a British daily newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: The Daily Telegraph is a national British newspaper, usually called simply a paper.

clue.text: Farm occupant knocked back beer in car close to henhouse

indicators.note: close means the end, so the last letter of henhouse
knocked back means turned back, so the car with beer inside reads backwards
the beer word goes within the car word

parts.note: BMW is a German make of car
ale is a type of beer

explanation.surface: Someone downed a beer in the car parked near the henhouse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'knocked back' looks like drinking the beer; it reverses the car with the beer inside, giving the first six letters, before the henhouse's last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A ewe lamb is a young female sheep, a natural inhabitant of a farm.

clue.text: Susan outside able to fabricate aquamarine

indicators.note: the name goes round the other letters

parts.note: Sue is the short form of Susan

indicators.note: to fabricate is to make up, so the letters are reworked

explanation.surface: Susan is not able to make up a gemstone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to fabricate' rearranges the given word into EABL, which goes inside the short name.
explanation.definitionFit: Aquamarine is a pale greenish-blue colour, like that of the sea, so sea-blue matches it.

clue.text: Cheers baby, when dropping in

indicators.note: the time word drops inside the baby word

parts.note: a tot is a small child
as means when, as in 'as he left'

explanation.surface: A drinking salute as a baby drops by.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cheers' looks like an exclamation of thanks; here it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A toast is the drinking salute itself, said when glasses are raised, like the call of cheers.

clue.text: Top-class crumble and pastry served up where Italians eat

indicators.note: in a down clue 'up' means the whole run is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: A1 means first-rate, written here with the letter I for the figure 1
to rot is to crumble away
a tart is a pastry

explanation.surface: Excellent crumble and tart dished up at an Italian restaurant.
explanation.walkthrough: AI + ROT + TART read upwards gives the answer. 'crumble' and 'pastry' look like desserts.
explanation.definitionFit: A trattoria is an informal Italian restaurant serving simple food, so it is a place for Italian eating.

clue.text: Monstrous annual rut is broadcast

indicators.note: broadcast seed is scattered widely, so these letters are scattered

explanation.surface: The yearly rutting season is shown on TV as something monstrous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is broadcast' rearranges ANNUAL RUT.
explanation.definitionFit: Something monstrous is abnormal and against nature, which is what unnatural means.

clue.text: One interrupts broadcast on Wagner and Grieg perhaps

indicators.note: the single letter breaks into the rearranged letters
broadcast means scattered widely, so the letters are scattered

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: Someone interrupts a radio programme about the composers Wagner and Grieg.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broadcast' rearranges the fodder into NORWEGAN, which the single letter then interrupts.
explanation.definitionFit: Edvard Grieg was a composer from Norway, so an example of a person of that nationality.

clue.text: Strict EU operative with oil rigs

indicators.note: operative means working, so these letters are worked over into a new order

explanation.surface: An EU agent works on oil rigs and is a stickler for the rules.
explanation.walkthrough: 'operative' rearranges EU + OIL RIGS. 'with' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Religious can mean scrupulous or meticulous, as in following a routine religiously, so strict.

clue.text: Listen to Shakespeare character choking halfway through lines — like Hamlet?

indicators.note: the king is choking on the inserted letters, which are stuck inside him

parts.note: King Lear is the title character of a Shakespeare tragedy

indicators.note: the letter halfway through the word lines is its middle one

parts.note: Hamlet was a Prince of Denmark, so a Dane

explanation.surface: An actor playing Lear chokes halfway through his lines, like Hamlet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' is a link. 'Shakespeare character' and 'Hamlet' tempt one to look for a single play; Hamlet only supplies his nationality.
explanation.definitionFit: To lend an ear is an idiom meaning to pay attention and hear someone out.

clue.text: Outsiders in league playing in game somewhere in France

indicators.note: the outside letters of league are its first and last
the versus letter goes within the animal word

parts.note: hare is hunted as game
V, short for versus, is used for one team playing another

explanation.surface: Outsiders in a league are playing in a match somewhere in France.
explanation.walkthrough: LE + HA(V)RE. 'game' looks like a match; here it is hunted animals.
explanation.definitionFit: Le Havre is a port city in Normandy in northern France.

clue.text: Depression, then gold brings brightness in US

parts.note: a col is a dip between mountain peaks
or is the heraldic word for gold

explanation.surface: After a low point, gold brings lustre in America.
explanation.walkthrough: 'then' is a link; 'in US' points to the American spelling without U.
explanation.definitionFit: Colour can mean vividness or brilliance of hue, so brightness; the US spelling drops the U.

clue.text: Vegetable survives in hard ground

indicators.note: the existence word goes inside the rearranged letters
ground means crushed and broken up, so the letters are reordered

parts.note: is means exists or survives

explanation.surface: A vegetable lasts in hard soil.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ground' rearranges the given word into RADH. 'ground' looks like soil, and 'hard ground' like a description of it.
explanation.definitionFit: A radish is a crisp red root vegetable eaten raw.

clue.text: Non-conformist in charge after sacking 3

indicators.note: the charge abbreviation comes after the rearranged number
sacking a town wrecks it, so the letters are wrecked into a new order

parts.note: the figure 3 written as a word

explanation.surface: A rebel takes charge after firing three people.
explanation.walkthrough: '3' looks like a cross-reference to clue 3; it is just the word three, which 'sacking' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: A heretic holds opinions at odds with accepted doctrine, so is a nonconformist.

clue.text: Record registered in rhubarb plant again?

indicators.note: to be registered in something is to be entered within it

parts.note: rhubarb and rot both mean nonsense
EP is an extended-play record

explanation.surface: A record is entered in the rhubarb section of the plant show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rhubarb' looks like the plant but means nonsense. The question mark marks a definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: To repot is to move a plant into another pot, a way of planting it again.

clue.text: Spiteful, garrulous, hard to miss

indicators.note: the talkative word has to go without a letter

parts.note: garrulous means chatty
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: Someone spiteful and talkative is hard to overlook.
explanation.walkthrough: CHATTY without H gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Catty means sly and malicious in remarks, the same as spiteful.

clue.text: Mad final required loose gear

indicators.note: required here suggests the end word is needed to hold the other letters within it

parts.note: end means final part

indicators.note: loose means free and slack, so the letters are freed to rearrange

explanation.surface: A cup final requires loose kit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loose' rearranges the fodder into RAGE, which the final word holds. 'final' looks like a cup match.
explanation.definitionFit: Mad in the sense of furious or very angry, as enraged means.

clue.text: Star cook finishes in the capital

parts.note: to cook the books is to rig them

indicators.note: the finishing letters of the following words are taken

explanation.surface: A star chef finishes work in the capital.
explanation.walkthrough: RIG + E and L, the last letters of 'the' and 'capital'. 'Star cook' looks like a celebrity chef.
explanation.definitionFit: Rigel is the brightest star in the constellation Orion.

clue.text: Transferred to private boats in Venice

indicators.note: transferred means moved about, so the letters are moved into a new order

explanation.surface: Moved to private boats in Venice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Transferred' rearranges TO PRIVATE.
explanation.definitionFit: Vaporetti are Venice's motorised water-buses, the plural of vaporetto.

clue.text: Description of crude crossword? The result of a 12 x 12 construction

definitions.meaning: a vulgar puzzle could be called coarse or vulgar

definitions.text: The result of a 12 x 12 construction
definitions.meaning: twelve twelves make 144, an old unit of quantity

explanation.surface: A rude puzzle might be built on a twelve-by-twelve grid.
explanation.definitionFit: Gross means both vulgar or coarse and a quantity of twelve dozen.

clue.text: Language course around London?

parts.note: a course read as the course of a river near London, where its mouth meets the sea, and the speech of that area

explanation.surface: An English class held in the London area.
explanation.walkthrough: 'course' looks like lessons but is the river Thames's course into its tidal mouth. The accent of the south-east of England takes its name from the Thames mouth.
explanation.definitionFit: This accent is a form of speech from the Thames area, blending London and standard pronunciation.
